questions.q: What does Flow Designer's native If/Else construct let you do?
options: Branch a flow into one of two paths of actions based on whether a condition evaluates true or false, with no scripting
Write a server-side Business Rule in JavaScript
Delete a record conditionally from within a Notify action
Combine two separate flows into one
questions.explain: If/Else is a visual, no-code branching construct native to Flow Designer.

questions.q: A condition is built using which pattern?
options: A free-text script block
Field, operator, value -- the same structure used by ACL conditions and list filters
A fixed list of ServiceNow-defined scenarios with no customization
A drag-and-drop flowchart with no actual comparison
questions.explain: The field/operator/value condition builder is reused across ACLs, list filters, and Flow Designer's If/Else.

questions.q: An If/Else condition checks "Priority is Critical." An incoming incident has Priority set to High. Which branch runs?
options: The If branch
Both branches run in sequence
The Else branch
Neither branch runs and the flow stops
questions.explain: Since "High" does not equal "Critical," the condition evaluates false, so the Else branch runs.

questions.q: Can an If/Else's two branches contain different numbers and types of steps?
options: No, both branches must mirror each other exactly
No, only the If branch is allowed to contain steps
Yes, each branch runs its own independent sequence of actions, and they don't have to reconverge
Only if a subflow is used instead
questions.explain: Each branch is independent -- one might send an urgent SMS and create a task, the other might just send a standard email.

questions.q: Before Flow Designer, where did this kind of branching logic typically live?
options: It was not possible to implement at all in ServiceNow
In a Business Rule or Script Include written in server-side JavaScript
Only in a scheduled job with no condition logic
In a static HTML page
questions.explain: If/Else gives administrators the same decision-making power that previously required a developer writing server-side script.
